S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

symptom.disease_info: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder is defined by intrusive, unwanted obsessions and/or repetitive compulsions performed to reduce distress or prevent feared outcomes, with the cycle becoming time-consuming or functionally impairing. Its course often fluctuates with stress and responsibility, and it is distinguished from ordinary worry or perfectionism by the unwanted, repetitive, excessive quality of the thoughts and acts and the person’s difficulty disengaging from them.

patient.stressor: After Sophia was fired from a design agency during a tense client turnover, she treated the loss as a warning that every draft, file, and presentation had to be protected from even the smallest possible error. At first this looked like professional diligence, but intrusive doubts about her work began prompting repeated reviewing, re-saving, and mentally retracing design decisions even when she knew the extra steps were excessive. She remained employed as a designer, but the pattern started to narrow her creative spontaneity, strain deadlines, and make the pursuit of a creative director role feel increasingly precarious. Sophia sought psychiatric care on her own after realizing that her usual stress outlets—yoga, gardening, and gallery visits—were no longer enough to keep the work rituals from interfering with her career.

S065.manifestation: I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout or sent the wrong version to a client, and even when I can see it’s probably fine, my mind keeps circling back to it.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: Before I submit work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes mentally walk through every design choice one more time, which doesn’t take over my whole day but does make me slower and less free creatively.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still getting my work done, but I’ve started missing internal deadlines and holding back on bolder design ideas because I’m afraid I’ll overlook something and damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role.
